newsitem.title: USA: Calif. panel OKs bill to restore local funding.
newsitem.headline: Calif. panel OKs bill to restore local funding.

text.p: A California legislative panel on Wednesday approved a bill that would restore billions of dollars in funding to local governments, state lawmakers said.

The Assembly Local Government Committee, on a bipartisan vote, approved Assembly Bill 95, by Assemblyman Fred Aguiar. The bill, if backed by the legislature and signed by Gov. Pete Wilson, would eventually restore $3.5 billion annually to local governments in the state.
"Local governments are in dire need of relief," Aguiar said. "Putting an end to the state's annual property tax take-away will place local governments on the road to recovery. It's long overdue."
In 1992, the state began to siphon property taxes from local governments in an attempt to balance its own budget.

Local governments, regardless of their financial health, were required to place a portion of these locally collected revenues into the newly created Educational Revenue Augmentation Fund, known as ERAF.

The state used these funds to cover its own financial obligation to schools. The size of local governments' contribution to the fund has grown each year, and is currently estimated to be $3.5 billion annually.

Aguiar's bill would initially cap ERAF contributions at the 1996-1997 level, and then reduce the fund to zero over a period of 10 years. This plan would effectively return $350 million to California local governments each year.
The bill would require the state to backfill any fiscal impact on California schools.
